messages.subject: Cannot find the selected parameter in the cal_parms.cal file
messages.subject_clean: Cannot find the selected parameter in the cal_parms.cal file
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am encountering a persistent issue in RSWAT v4.01 (Shiny) when using a SWAT+ project.

When I click “Check input table” in Parameter sampling, I always get the error:
>
> Error: Cannot find the selected parameter in the cal_parms.cal file

This happens even for a single parameter and after extensive checks.
Details:

SWAT+ project (SWAT+ rev. 61.0.x)

RSWAT version: v4.01

Operating system: Windows

Parameter file: cal_parms.cal generated by SWAT+ Editor v3.x
What I have verified / tried:

The parameter name is exactly identical to the name column in cal_parms.cal (e.g. cn2).

The correct object type is used (e.g. cn2 → hru).

I tested with only one parameter (cn2) in the table.

I removed the descriptive first line from cal_parms.cal (the “written by SWAT+ editor …” line).

I restarted RSWAT and reloaded the project.

I also tested a cleaned, tab-delimited version of cal_parms.cal (no fixed-width formatting).

The error persists in all cases.
Please see also the attache file.

Thank you very much for your help in advance.

With kind regards,
Majid

messages.subject: RSWAT SUFI-2 error: 'no lines available in input' (print.prt checked)
messages.subject_clean: RSWAT SUFI-2 error: 'no lines available in input' (print.prt checked)
messages.body_plain:
I am currently running SWAT+ with RSWAT (SUFI-2) without the GUI and encountering a persistent issue.
The SWAT+ simulations complete successfully, but during RSWAT post-processing I repeatedly get:
> Error in { : task X failed - "no lines available in input"
I have verified that:
print.prt has all outputs set to y, including channel_sd with daily output
channel_sd exists in the TxtInOut folder
time.sim is properly defined (daily step, correct simulation years)
channel_sd_day.txt is generated, but some simulations contain only headers (no numeric rows)
When the model does run, all extracted output variables (e.g., flo_out) are zero (in the working folder -inside the core-x)
Even after detecting and re-running those failed simulations, the error still occurs intermittently.
Is there a recommended way to skip failed simulations?
Thank you very much for your time and help.
Best regards,
Mahabub

messages.subject: Re: Error: "no lines available in input"
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I am running SWAT+ using RSWAT and encountering an error during the calibration workflow, even though the SWAT+ simulation itself runs without any problem.

Simulation status:

SWAT+ run completes successfully

Console message: “Execution successfully completed”

Output files (e.g., channel_sd_day.txt) are generated

print.prt and file.cio have been checked and look correct

Error in RSWAT:
Error in { : task 2 failed - "no lines available in input"

When it happens:

Task 1 (model execution) completes successfully

The error occurs in task 2, when RSWAT tries to read outputs / calculate the objective function

What I have already checked:

Output variables are enabled in print.prt

Simulation period and output frequency are correct in file.cio

SWAT+ executable runs correctly outside RSWAT

Output files are not empty and can be opened manually

I reviewed RSWAT FAQ #1 (SWAT+: constant objective function values?) and the related YouTube guidance.  Has anyone experienced this error?
Thanks

> > > On Friday, November 29, 2024 at 1:58:58 PM UTC Alfa Essossinam wrote:
> > > > I think the problem is from the range that has been set for each parameter at Step2.
> > > > When using parallel processing, you would notice some core(s) run till the end but others do not. Those that stop are those where at least one parameter value sampled is out of bound. To solve the problem, open your wolkingFolder/output then "CurrentSimulationReport.log". From there you can determine the core(s) that could not achieve it's simulation. Open the TxtInOut_x corresponding, then calibration.cal, there you will see the values sampled for each parameter. You can use your experience to determine the parameter(s) and the value(s) out of bound or start deleting parameters (the whole line) one at a time and running  the model using the executable which is already in the TxtInOut_x folder. It will keep failling until the parameter(s) out of bound is (are) removed. Once the parameter(s) out of bound is determined adjust the value until SWAT (executable) could run properly. Reajust the range then and restart the process at Step2. The parameter out of bound in my case was bd.sol
> > > >
> > > > I hope this would help, good luck.
